planned_path.path_summary: Use the authorized wage gain table to estimate whether immigrants with no high school experience have larger log wage gains at migration than immigrants with a college degree, adjusting for available demographic and source-country differences.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Use observations in the authorized wage_gain_table file with positive adjusted wages and education in the never-high-school or college-degree categories.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for missing/non-finite outcome, predictor, or controls.
path_signature.variable_construction: Log-transform adjusted wages, difference logs to form log wage gain, classify education groups, create demographic controls, and use country fixed effects.
path_signature.inference_rule: The claim is supported if the never_high_school coefficient is positive, with p < 0.05 treated as clear statistical support.

analysis_path.path_description: Use the authorized wage gain table to estimate whether immigrants with no high school experience have larger log wage gains at migration than immigrants with a college degree, adjusting for available demographic and source-country differences.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/Hendricks_QuartJournEco_2018_wNKW/test/data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Convert edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, yearLastUsJob, yrborn, and sex to numeric as needed.
Create log_home_wage = log(lastHomeWageAdjusted) and log_us_wage = log(lastUsWageAdjusted).
Create log_wage_gain = log_us_wage - log_home_wage.
Create age_at_us_job = yearLastUsJob - yrborn.
Create female = 1 for sex == 2 and 0 for sex == 1.
Classify education as never_high_school if edyrs < 9, college_degree if edyrs >= 16, and other_education otherwise.
Keep observations with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages, finite log_wage_gain, and education group equal to never_high_school or college_degree.
Set college_degree as the reference category.
Estimate OLS regression of log_wage_gain on education group, female, age_at_us_job, age_at_us_job squared, and country fixed effects.
Report the coefficient for never_high_school relative to college_degree, its standard error, p-value, confidence interval, and percent difference 100*(exp(coef)-1).

key_choices.outcome_measure: Log wage gain from migration, computed as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Education group indicator comparing edyrs < 9 against edyrs >= 16.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Use observations in the authorized wage_gain_table file with positive adjusted wages and education in the never-high-school or college-degree categories.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No explicit trimming; log transformation is used to reduce leverage from wage-scale extremes.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for missing/non-finite outcome, predictor, or controls.
key_choices.data_processing: Log-transform adjusted wages, difference logs to form log wage gain, classify education groups, create demographic controls, and use country fixed effects.
key_choices.model_choice: OLS linear regression on log wage gain.
key_choices.inference_rule: The claim is supported if the never_high_school coefficient is positive, with p < 0.05 treated as clear statistical support.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ edu_group + female + age_at_us_job + I(age_at_us_job^2) + factor(country)
models.planned_estimation: Coefficient for edu_groupnever_high_school relative to college_degree; percent difference computed as 100*(exp(coefficient)-1).
models.inference_criteria: Positive coefficient indicates larger wage gains for never-high-school immigrants; p < 0.05 indicates statistically significant support.
models.qualification: A log wage gain regression directly estimates the education difference in proportional gains, and demographic/source-country controls are standard observational adjustments available in the dataset.

outcome.name: log_wage_gain
outcome.definition: Difference between log adjusted U.S. wage and log adjusted home-country wage for each immigrant.
outcome.variable_construction: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), after requiring both adjusted wage variables to be positive.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Drop observations with missing, non-positive, or non-finite adjusted wages or non-finite log_wage_gain.
outcome.qualification: The claim concerns gains on migration; log wage differences measure proportional wage gains, which match statements such as gaining a percentage more.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.definition: Categorical education group comparing immigrants who have never been to high school with immigrants with a college degree.
main_predictor.variable_construction: never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16; other education groups excluded from the focal comparison.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Drop observations missing edyrs or outside the two focal groups for this model.
main_predictor.qualification: The focal claim explicitly compares immigrants who have never been to high school with those with a college degree.

controls.name: female
controls.variable_construction: female = 1 if sex == 2; female = 0 if sex == 1.
controls.missing_data_handling: Drop observations with missing or unrecognized sex values.
controls.qualification: Sex is an available demographic predictor of wages and helps adjust for compositional differences between education groups.

controls.name: age_at_us_job
controls.definition: Approximate age at the last U.S. job observation.
controls.missing_data_handling: Drop observations with missing or non-finite age_at_us_job.
controls.qualification: Age proxies labor-market experience and lifecycle wage differences.

controls.name: I(age_at_us_job^2)
controls.missing_data_handling: Drop observations with missing or non-finite age_at_us_job.
controls.qualification: The quadratic term allows a nonlinear age-wage profile.

controls.name: factor(country)
controls.definition: Country fixed effects for source country.
controls.variable_construction: Use country as a categorical factor.
controls.qualification: Country fixed effects compare education groups within source-country categories and adjust for source-country composition.

expected_outputs: Coefficient, standard error, t statistic, p-value, and 95% confidence interval for never_high_school versus college_degree.
Percent difference in wage gain computed as 100*(exp(coefficient)-1).
Analytic sample counts by education group.

analysis_code.notes: No original analysis code was found in the authorized folder. This planning-created R script contains both Task1 and Task2 analyses and should be executed later without changing the analysis design.

pruning_review.reason: Task1 is high-quality. The original paper is observational and studies individual immigrants' pre- and post-migration wages, including the focal education comparison that less educated immigrants gain more on migration than college graduates. The authorized dataset has 2,854 individual-immigrant rows, contains the required education, adjusted home wage, adjusted U.S. wage, sex, age-construction, and country variables, and has no individual ID suggesting repeated person-level observations. The code reads only the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx, constructs log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted)-log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), classifies edyrs < 9 versus edyrs >= 16, fits the planned OLS model with female, age, age squared, and country fixed effects, and prints the focal coefficient and counts. No Rule 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.6, or 1.7 defect is present. The dataset has extreme wage values, especially lastHomeWageAdjusted, but the plan acknowledges wage-scale extremes and uses a log transformation; without authorized evidence that this materially changes the focal conclusion, Rule 1.5 is not triggered and guardrails G8 and G14 apply. Verification limitation: as required for pruning, I did not execute the code or inspect any expected/human review result.

pruning_review.reason: Task2 is high-quality. The case-specific instruction requires the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the supplied NIS/Migration Projects wage-gain table, including Mexico, and no sector or rural/urban region controls. The authorized dataset is described as that pooled poor-country table and includes Mexico as the dominant country category. The code uses the same authorized file, retains all countries including Mexico, restricts only to the focal education groups with positive adjusted wages, constructs the requested log wage gain, fits log_wage_gain ~ edu_group with no controls, and does not use occupation variables as sector proxies. Thus Rules 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, and 2.5 are not triggered. The absence of controls is required for Task2, and a different model from Task1 is allowed under guardrail G3. Extreme wage values are present, but the log transformation is justified and no authorized evidence shows material harm to the requested comparable result, so Rule 2.7/1.5 is not triggered. Verification limitation: I reviewed the linked code but did not execute it or read any forbidden expected/human-review result.
